reserveReview.rationale: The reviewed staking documentation identifies wiTRY as ERC-4626 shares in deposited iTRY. The live adapter already pins the exact Ethereum iTRY asset; admitting itry-brix makes that direct claim a tracked 100% wrapper dependency. The source key and high legacy risk remain unchanged. DLF fund constituents and custody uncertainty belong to the parent reserve review and remain inherited; linking the immediate iTRY claim does not establish fund look-through or a complete cross-chain reserve/liability census. Current pinned asset() and totalAssets() at Ethereum block 26423424 corroborate the adapter-owned claim identity. The October 1 composition and separately retained October report keep their original clocks; November 15 identity corroboration and parent linking do not renew those holdings or report observations.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Retained October 1 ERC-4626 single-asset claim; November 15 exact underlying identity review links the newly tracked parent without renewing holdings evidence
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The direct reserve instrument is fully identified as iTRY. Unknown DLF constituents, custody safeguards and final redemption capacity remain inherited from the parent rather than treated as resolved look-through.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Brix names Zodia Custody as the institutional custodian of the underlying reserves, while the staking contracts hold iTRY for the wrapper. Brix does not publish provider shares or establish legal segregation, insolvency remoteness, or collateral reuse restrictions. The British Virgin Islands disclosure identifies wiTRY Limited, not the on-chain contracts or Zodia.
